newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian authorities question tobacco firm chief.
newsitem.headline: Indian authorities question tobacco firm chief.

text.p: Indian authorities said they questioned the chairman of the country's biggest tobacco firm on Thursday after the arrests of four people who authorities allege violated foreign exchange rules.
A senior official of India's Enforcement Directorate said it had questioned ITC Ltd Chairman Yogesh Deveshwar and that Deveshwar's house had been searched.
"Deveshwar is being interrogated. His house has been searched in the morning," the official, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters.
The questioning of Deveshwar and the search followed Wednesday's arrest of an executive director and three former ITC executives who were later taken into custody until November 13.

The Enforcement Directorate said on Wednesday it had enough evidence showing that ITC, which is 31.67 percent controlled by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc, had violated foreign exchange rules in the amount of $112 million.
The directorate accused ITC of colluding with an unspecified U.S.-based firm to show inflated profits.
K.K. Kabirpanthi, deputy director of the directorate, told a news conference on Wednesday the violations had begun in 1991.
Saurav Misra, a deputy chairman of the firm, and former chairman J.N. Sapru were also called for interrogation on Wednesday, the official said.
ITC's share price, however, stabilised on Thursday after falling more than 18 rupees to 303 on Wednesday on the Bombay bourse. On Thursday, it moved in a narrow range to close a rupee higher at 304.
"It is a good time to buy ITC," said Sujay Mishra, company analyst at SSKI Securities. "Crises like this offer buy opportunities at cheap valuations."
The Enforcement Directorate said on Wednesay it did not rule out more arrests.
An executive of a British investment bank said more arrests could lead to a management shakeout in ITC.
"It will be a good opportunity for B.A.T to seek majority control in the company," said the executive, speaking anonymously.
Two years ago, B.A.T wanted to increase its stake in ITC, which controls more than 65 percent of India's tobacco market, a move that was strongly opposed by former chairman K.L. Chugh.

The Finance Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday that the searches were conducted "only after sufficient evidence had been collected indicating FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act) violations by ITC Ltd to the tune of over $100 million".
ITC has not commented publicly on the investigation.
